channel.title: Wire — Programming
channel.description: Programming from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: A new Go API for JSON
item.description: Go 1.27 introduces new encoding/json/v2 and encoding/json/jsontext packages. (2 sources: goblog, lobsters)

item.title: Discord is ditching Electron and its new app uses less RAM
item.description: Discord is moving its apps fully over to the Rust programming language. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Leapwork Play Reaches GA with Governance for Playwright Tests
item.description: Leapwork Play adds requirement traceability and approval workflows around portable Playwright tests. Full governance and audit capabilities require an enterprise package. By Mark Silvester (1 source: infoq)

item.title: How I built a ’90s-style adventure game on top of my Hugo blog
Safari introduces Adaptive Dark Mode in 27.3
item.description: We’re excited to announce Adaptive Dark Mode in Safari 27.3 beta. (3 sources: frontendfocus, hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: Burnt TOAST: Why DBAs Dread Large Text Columns
item.description: Shaun Thomas on how PostgreSQL TOAST stores large columns, when it speeds up scans and updates, and where splitting a table or switching to lz4 helps - with benchmarks. (2 sources: lobsters, postgresweekly)

item.title: Motorola Signature 27 with GrapheneOS support
item.description: Meet motorola signature 27, Motorola's most advanced flagship smartphone ever with next-gen AI, industry-leading tech, & a distnctive design. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: sshole
item.description: openssh on musl linux has been letting people into password-less accounts since 2016. (2 sources: hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: Residential proxies detected on White House network
item.description: Our Residential Proxy Observatory shows residential proxy traffic exiting the White House network (AS2650) 236 times in 30 days, through 28 proxy services. (2 sources: hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: A thousand fewer paths to root
We now have Kerr’s Law
item.description: Dave Kerr created hacker laws, and now he finds himself reviewing agent-written code for them. (1 source: changelog)
